messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

Here's a draft. The bracketed figures are placeholders — swap in your real numbers, because the argument only lands if the counts are yours.

---

**Proposal: one quarter of engineering time for debt paydown**

**Ask:** Dedicate Q[X] to paying down debt in [the billing service and the shared auth layer]. No new roadmap features from the [N]-person platform team for those twelve weeks.

**Why now.** Our median PR now takes [4.5] days from open to merge, up from [1.8] a year ago. CI takes [38] minutes and fails spuriously about [one run in six], so people stop trusting it and merge on a re-run. Three of our last five Sev-2 incidents traced back to the same untested config path in billing. We are paying for this quarter's debt whether or not we schedule it — currently we pay in unplanned incident weekends and in features that slip twice before landing.

**What we'd do.** Split the config path into something with a test harness around it. Retire the [2016-era] job runner that only [two engineers] can safely touch. Cut CI to under [15] minutes by parallelizing the integration suite.

**What we'd measure.** Median PR merge time, CI wall-clock, spurious failure rate, and Sev-2 count — reported weekly, baseline captured before we start. If merge time hasn't moved by week eight, we stop and reassess rather than finish the plan on principle.

**The cost.** [Two] roadmap items slip a quarter: [feature A] and [feature B]. Both are worth less than the interest we're paying.

I'd rather do this now than negotiate for it after the next incident.

---

~250 words. Tell me the real numbers and the actual systems and I'll tighten it into a version you can send.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
